**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Tomato (green unripe tomatoes visible in background)
- **Affected part**: Leaves, multiple leaflets
- **Key features**:
  - Large, irregular brown-to-tan necrotic blotches covering substantial leaf area
  - Distinct pale greenish-gray halos/borders surrounding the necrotic zones
  - Lesions appear dry and papery in texture
  - Damage originates at leaf margins and tips, progressing inward
  - Some whitish/pale material visible at affected zones (possible sporulation)
  - No concentric rings evident (rules out Early Blight)
  - No small discrete spots with yellow halos (rules out Septoria, Bacterial Speck)

**Reasoning through top candidates:**

- **Late Blight**: "brown patches of dead tissue surrounded by a pale green or gray border... lesions are brown and papery... leaf lesions surrounded by distinctive pale green or gray halos." This matches very well — large irregular brown patches with clearly visible pale halos on tomato.
- **Gray Mold**: Also shows V-shaped blotches from margins, but key indicator is fluffy gray spore mass; no dense gray sporulation clearly visible here.
- **Verticillium Wilt**: V-shaped lesions at margins with yellowing surrounds — plausible, but Verticillium typically shows more pronounced yellowing and vascular discoloration, not the clear pale halos seen here.

The pale greenish-gray halos around large brown papery necrotic patches on tomato leaves is the most distinctive feature, pointing strongly to **Late Blight**.
